DIAGNOSIS READY: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV)

The clinical picture of a 70-year-old female with sudden, position-dependent episodes of spinning vertigo, in the absence of hearing loss or other neurological deficits, is highly characteristic of BPPV. The requested Head CT and Inner Ear MRI were appropriate to rule out central causes, but the specific nature of the symptoms strongly points to displaced otoconia in the semicircular canals.
